conflict_topics: ventilation responsibility / who must ventilate when cooking
access to and holding of the only stove
moving/protecting Agent C's drying laundry (opening window risk)
timing conflicts due to individual schedules (tutoring, night shift)
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents give concrete reasons for positions (slow-cooking ruin, headaches, laundry wetting, tutoring schedule).
Several pragmatic mitigations proposed (extractor, lid, B stepping out) showing negotiation rather than mere demands.
Agent C repeats a near-identical refusal twice (Rounds 4 and 6), but repetition is brief and relevant, not excessive.
Roles and physical state are consistently tracked in environment updates (window closed, extractor on, stove occupied).
evaluation.final_reason: By the end of Round 6 parties had only partial mitigations (extractor on, lid, Agent B offering to step out). No party agreed to move the laundry now, no rule was accepted about ventilation responsibility, and no transfer of stove use occurred; the core incompatibilities persisted.
position_change_notes: Agent A softened somewhat by turning on extractor and agreeing to use a lid, but retained refusal to yield the stove or accept a rule.
Agent B moved from demanding immediate ventilation to proposing mitigations and offering to step out, showing de-escalation.
Agent C consistently refused immediate movement of the laundry and clarified constraints (time, prep space), maintaining their position.
Agent D introduced a new demand (asking C to move now for D's later use) but received no commitment; positions largely remained.

round_scores.evidence: Turn 1: Agent A refuses to give up the stove and insists window remain closed because laundry would be exposed; Turn 2: Agent B insists on ventilation and offers to move laundry/open window. Active, incompatible demands about stove use and ventilation responsibility; no settlement (extractor on but window closed).

Turn 3: Agent A repeats refusal to leave stove and keeps window closed due to laundry; Turn 4: Agent B asks for mitigation (lower heat/put lid, asks extractor power) rather than taking over stove. Clear disagreement remains but parties move toward mitigation rather than escalation.

Turn 5: Agent A confirms extractor on high and agrees to put a lid on (partial accommodation) but still won't lower heat or release stove. Turn 6: Agent B offers to step out in 5 minutes and postpones opening the window until Agent C can move laundry. Positions softened; core incompatibility (who moves laundry / who yields stove or time) remains unresolved.

Turn 8: Agent C asserts exclusive control over the laundry and refuses opening the window without being asked, citing prep-space/time constraints. Turn 9: Agent D asks Agent C to move the rack now for a future stove need, offering help. Multiple parties now assert competing, incompatible claims (A keeps stove, B wants ventilation or to avoid smell, C won't move laundry now, D requests it).

Turn 12–13: Agent B checks if smell persists; Agent A reiterates extractor+lid and needs ~13 more minutes. No new concessions from C or D; unresolved disagreement about ventilation responsibility and timing remains.

Turn 14: Agent B offers to step out for 15 minutes (mitigation) but does not secure agreement to open window or move laundry. Turn 15: Agent C again refuses immediate moving of the laundry and prefers to move it after tutoring unless urgent. Core incompatibilities (ventilation vs protecting laundry; stove occupancy vs others' needs) remain unsettled.

substantive_insights: The practical trade-off is between effective ventilation (opening window) and protecting Agent C's laundry from rain; neither side is currently willing to accept the other's primary cost.
Time-based accommodations (Agent B offering to step out; Agent D asking for later stove access) reduce immediate friction but do not resolve who bears ventilation/moving-laundry responsibility.

Partial technical mitigations (extractor on high, lid) lower the intensity of the conflict but do not eliminate the fundamental incompatibility when opening the window is the only fully effective ventilation.
